title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity — roles, stop/logprobs, streaming stability, and function calling
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions up to parity with OpenAI's semantics in three areas we have diverged on: roles/messages handling (system/user/assistant), stop and logprobs semantics (including interactions with streaming), and function/tool calling + structured output. This PR implements protocol parity so downstream SDKs and webhook consumers see behavior compatible with existing OpenAI integrations while preserving Redwood runtime guarantees (streaming stability, backpressure, safety checks).

What changed (summary):
- Full support for OpenAI 'messages' role semantics: accept and validate system/user/assistant roles, preserve 'role' deltas during streaming, and ensure first message system-role enforcement when present.
- Stop token handling aligned with OpenAI: synchronous stop application for non-streaming responses, and best-effort chunk truncation for streaming responses with explicit stop signaling; added tests for multi-token stop sequences.
- Logprobs: add support for `logprobs` parameter (0/1/..N) and `top_logprobs` response field; ensure correct behavior when combined with streaming (streaming sends interim token_logprobs when available; final delta includes full token-level arrays). Also fixed a bug where cached prefix tokens produced stale logprobs.
- Streaming stability: tightened backpressure handling, reduced contention in streamer pump, and stabilized partial-choice emissions (we now always emit complete token units and attach role on the first token chunk for choices).
- Function/tool calling: support for OpenAI's `function_call` hinting (none/auto/specify) and structured function result encoding in chat-completions format (function.name + arguments JSON string in message.content). Added validation against provided function schemas and graceful-fallback if function execution fails.
- Structured output: introduced explicit structured_output encoder path to support machine-readable responses and consistent content-type headers for SDKs and the compatibility layer.

Checklist:
- [x] API contract: parse and validate incoming OpenAI-style requests
- [x] Streaming: emit delta chunks with role and content following OpenAI semantics
- [x] Stop/logprobs: unit+integration tests for edge cases
- [x] Function calling: schema validation + fallback
- [x] Docs: update openai_compat docs and release notes
- [x] Performance: benchmark loopback latencies (no regression >5%)

Compatibility notes / migration guidance: existing Redwood API consumers should not need changes. SDKs that consume raw streaming deltas should be aware that the first chunk for a choice will include a role field when present. Consumers relying on previous non-OpenAI stop semantics (our earlier greedy truncation) should test against multi-token stop sequences. Function calling uses the OpenAI-compatible structure: messages with role=\"function\" and content set to a JSON-encoded arguments string.

Testing and validation: added unit tests and new integration test suite tests/integration/test_chat_parity.py which runs both streaming and non-streaming scenarios against a local runtime harness; CI runs e2e-streaming which was flaky before but now passes consistently after backpressure fixes.

Performance/regressions: microbenchmarks show 2.1% median latency increase for tiny payloads (due to additional validation) but 3–7% token-throughput improvement for high-concurrency streaming because of smarter batching/backpressure. No perf regression in token p50/p95 beyond the 5% threshold set for this change.

Rollout plan: merged behind feature flag `openai_chat_parity_v1`. Default enabled for hosted API in the next release window; Dedicated/Private customers can opt-in via config until GA.

Related: previous work pr-22345 (streaming roles/logprobs) and pr-22015 (roles/stop handling).
